text:
mika: hi folks, newbie question. trying to speed up local backups so i mounted only the WAL dir `./pg_wal:/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal` instead of the whole data dir. Postgres crashes at init with `initdb: could not change permissions of directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal": Permission denied`. why does mounting just pg_wal blow up?

sam: welcome! :wave: Postgres insists on controlling permissions of the whole data tree during init. Mounting a single subpath can confuse initdb because it touches parent dirs and expects atomic control. On mac/windows the mount layer often prevents changing perms on the mounted subtree.

kevin: +1. Two safe patterns: 1) Mount the entire data dir (named volume recommended) so initdb can set up everything. 2) If you really need WAL on a separate volume, initialize the DB first (no WAL mount), then stop Postgres, move pg_wal into the mounted volume and update PGDATA/PG_WAL manually or use `pg_basebackup`/replication setup. Doing the chown trick before init rarely works for subpath mounts.

mika: ah ok. i wanted WAL separate to experiment with fast file-sync for WAL shipping. any quick local dev workaround?

sam: for local dev: use a named volume for the main data dir and a second named volume for WAL, then after DB init move the WAL into that volume from inside the running container (as postgres user). Example flow:
1) Start postgres with single named volume, let it init.
2) `docker run --rm -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data -v walvol:/wal alpine sh -c "mkdir -p /wal/pg_wal && chown -R 999:999 /wal/pg_wal && mv /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal.bak && ln -s /wal/pg_wal /var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal"`
This keeps host FS confusion out and uses volumes that the daemon manages.

kevin: also note: if you bind-mount from host, ensure the owner matches container postgres uid (usually 999) and perms = 700. But on mac/docker-desktop sometimes host chown doesn't map correctly for subpath mounts. So named volumes are simpler for experiments.

infra-bot: onboarding tip: our local dev docs recommend using named volumes for Postgres, and if you experiment with separate WAL/data volumes, perform the move after init to avoid initdb permission checks. See https://intranet.redwood.dev/dev-setup#pg-wal for details.

mika: great, i'll try the named-volume + move approach. thanks y'all, saved me from a weird rabbit hole :relieved:

sam: ping if you want to pair on the WAL flow; happy to help.

mika: will do, appreciate it!
